title: A connection can carry risk
hook: A route can have more than one consequence.

knows: Animals depend on features of their surroundings.
doesNotKnow: In a toy model, a corridor allows animals from two groups to meet. If one group carries a transmissible disease, what additional possibility must be considered?

misconception: A single observation or change determines the same outcome everywhere.
objective: In a toy model, a corridor allows animals from two groups to meet. If one group carries a transmissible disease, what additional possibility must be considered?

claims.text: In a toy model, a corridor allows animals from two groups to meet. If one group carries a transmissible disease, what additional possibility must be considered? The corridor in the second panel creates a possible connection between groups, one labeled as carrying a disease in the stipulated scenario. Contact can create opportunities for transmission. Actual spread depends on contacts, infection and other factors; it is not guaranteed.
claims.source: Stipulated illustrative scenario, not wildlife observations. Source lead, not checked: OpenStax Biology 2e, ecology, https://openstax.org/details/books/biology-2e

claims.text: The panels show a simplified illustrative scenario, not observations or measurements of real animals.
A new path allows two wildlife groups to meet. Why might disease surveillance be relevant? Contact between groups can create a chance of transmission, not a certainty.
